name: Ownership
definition: Leaders are owners. They think long term and do not sacrifice long-term value for short-term results. They act on behalf of the whole company, not just their own team. They never say "that's not my job."

rows.under: Gives up ownership without asking whether the customer or the company is better served. Fine as long as "someone" is on the hook.
rows.justRight: Knows what they own and what they do not. Inventories it. Looks for ways to make it better, including giving it to a better owner.
rows.over: Never lets go of anything, even when another owner would be better for customers. Treats other groups as threats.

rows.under: Passes the blame. Steals the credit.
rows.justRight: Everything they put their name next to, they are proud of.
rows.over: Acts like a sole proprietor. Owns everything. Cannot delegate.

rows.situation: Something blocks you and has no clear owner
rows.under: Blames the blocker. Avoids owning anything that is not already theirs.
rows.justRight: Takes responsibility for the unowned blocker and drives it to a real owner or a real fix.
rows.over: Takes over work that already has an owner, just because it is in the way.

rows.justRight: Works until the items they are responsible for are actually taken care of.
rows.over: Micromanages everyone else's work to make sure they are being good owners.

rows.situation: A dependency is late or broken
rows.under: Lets the dependency derail the work. Blames them. Does not try to fix what is broken.
rows.justRight: Owns the dependency and follows up. Escalates when needed. Still responsible for the outcome.
rows.over: Never gives the dependency the benefit of the doubt. Micromanages their work instead of setting an audit and letting them do the job.

rows.situation: A tough decision with a local vs company tradeoff
rows.under: Does not make the tough call. Lets what happens happen.
rows.justRight: Makes the call that is in the long-term interest of the customer, and therefore the company.
rows.over: Makes the short-term call that optimizes their team and hurts customers or other teams.

rows.under: Never thinks about the future. Downplays problems that will show up later.
rows.justRight: Makes big bets they believe will pay off long term. Examines the risks. Moves when they have enough information.
rows.over: Protects what they have. Treats any suggested change as a threat.

rows.situation: You see a problem outside your area
rows.under: Assumes someone else will take care of it.
rows.justRight: Points out the problem and stays until a fix is in place, in their area or not. Makes sure the problem stays solved.
rows.over: Points out other people's problems to gain control of their space. Cares more about enlarging what they own than solving it.
